subtopics.title: Work Done by a Constant Force
subtopics.description: Scalar product W = F . Delta r = F s cos(theta); geometric projection; positive, negative, and zero work conditions.

subtopics.title: Work Done by a Variable Force
subtopics.description: Line integral of force vector along trajectory W = int F . dr; 1D integral W = int F(x) dx; graphical interpretation as signed area under F-x curve.

subtopics.title: Work Done by an Ideal Spring Force
subtopics.description: Restoring force F_s = -k x; integration from x_i to x_f yielding W_s = -1/2 k (x_f^2 - x_i^2); external agent work W_ext = +1/2 k x^2.

subtopics.title: Work Done by Frictional Forces
subtopics.description: Static friction work (can be positive, negative, or zero depending on reference frame and contact point displacement); kinetic friction dissipative work always negative at interface.

subtopics.title: Kinetic Energy of a Particle
subtopics.description: Operational definition K = 1/2 m v^2 = p^2 / (2m); frame dependence of kinetic energy; scalar positive-definite character in any given inertial frame.

subtopics.title: Work-Energy Theorem in Inertial Frames
subtopics.description: Universal dynamical equivalence W_net = Delta K; summation over all forces (conservative, non-conservative, external, internal); derivation from Newton's Second Law.

subtopics.title: Work-Energy Theorem in Non-Inertial Reference Frames
subtopics.description: Generalization W_net + W_pseudo = Delta K_rel in accelerating frame of reference; pseudo-force work contribution.

topics.title: Potential Energy and Conservation of Mechanical Energy

subtopics.title: Conservative vs Non-Conservative Forces
subtopics.description: Path independence criterion; vanishing closed-loop line integral oint F . dr = 0; curl-free condition in 3D; dissipative non-conservative forces.

subtopics.title: Potential Energy Definition and Gradient Relation
subtopics.description: Differential definition dU = -F_c . dr; force as negative potential gradient F = -grad(U) or F_x = -dU/dx; arbitrary choice of zero-reference datum.

subtopics.title: Equilibrium Analysis from Potential Energy Curves
subtopics.description: Equilibrium condition dU/dx = 0; second derivative criterion: stable (d^2 U/dx^2 > 0), unstable (d^2 U/dx^2 < 0), neutral (d^2 U/dx^2 = 0); turning points where E_mech = U(x).

subtopics.title: Conservation of Total Mechanical Energy
subtopics.description: E_mech = K + U = constant when only conservative forces do work; general energy balance equation Delta E_mech = W_nc + W_ext.

subtopics.title: Average and Instantaneous Power
subtopics.description: Time rate of energy transfer P = dW/dt = F . v; average power P_avg = Delta W / Delta t; units of Watt and Horsepower.

subtopics.title: Vertical Circular Motion and Critical Velocities
subtopics.description: Non-uniform circular motion of particle tied to light string; conservation of energy combined with radial Newton's law; minimum bottom speed v_bot = sqrt(5 g R) and top speed v_top = sqrt(g R) for loop completion.

subtopics.title: String Slackening and Projectile Departure
subtopics.description: Condition for tension vanishing T = 0 in upper quadrant (pi/2 < theta < pi); departure into parabolic free-fall projectile motion.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Center of Mass Frame Kinetic Energy and Inelastic Collisions
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Multi-particle kinetic energy decomposition K = K_cm + K_rel, impulse, and restitution coefficient e belong to Chapter 5: Center of Mass.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Energy Conservation
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Rotational kinetic energy 1/2 I omega^2 and rolling without slipping belong to Chapter 6: Rotational Motion.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Universal Gravitational Potential Energy across Astronomical Scales
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Inverse-square potential energy U(r) = -G M m / r and escape speed from planets belong to Chapter 7: Gravitation.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Thermodynamic Heat, Internal Energy, and Dissipation into Thermal Reservoirs
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Microscopic internal energy Delta U = Q - W belongs to Chapter 11: Thermodynamics.

primary_sources.title: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma
primary_sources.role: Rigorous conceptual definitions of kinetic energy, work done by constant and variable forces, spring work, gravitational potential energy, mechanical energy conservation, power, and vertical circular motion looping conditions.

primary_sources.title: Fundamentals of Physics (Halliday, Resnick & Walker, 9th Ed)
primary_sources.coverage: Chapter 7: Kinetic Energy and Work (pp. 173-202) & Chapter 8: Potential Energy and Conservation of Energy (pp. 203-240)
primary_sources.role: Calculus-based work integrals, scalar products, spring work integration, potential energy curve reading, turning points, stable/unstable equilibrium, power F . v.

primary_sources.title: University Physics with Modern Physics (Young & Freedman, 13th Ed)
primary_sources.coverage: Chapter 6: Work and Kinetic Energy (pp. 205-239) & Chapter 7: Potential Energy and Energy Conservation (pp. 240-273)
primary_sources.role: Curved path line integrals, 3D potential gradient F = -grad(U), internal vs external work, work-energy theorem proof, energy diagrams.

primary_sources.title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. 1
primary_sources.coverage: Lecture 4: Conservation of Energy & Lectures 13-14: Work and Potential Energy
primary_sources.role: Foundational physical philosophy of energy conservation, operational non-existence of energy mechanisms, line integrals in gravitational fields.

primary_sources.title: Problems in General Physics by I.E. Irodov
primary_sources.coverage: Part 1, Section 1.3: Laws of Conservation of Energy, Momentum, and Angular Momentum (pp. 26-36)
primary_sources.role: Advanced potential wells, coupled mechanical systems, variable force work, critical velocity transitions.

primary_sources.title: JEE Main Rank Booster Mock Test 02
primary_sources.coverage: Vertical circular motion and power questions
